content.title: About
content.content: Chicken nuggets are small pieces of chicken breast that are breaded and fried or baked. They are popular as a quick snack and are commonly served in fast‑food restaurants, cafeterias, and at home.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial nugget recipe was developed in the United States in the 1970s.
Nuggets are often served with a variety of sauces: barbecue, honey‑mustard, cheese, and spicy.
In some countries they are called “chicken bites” or “chicken sticks.”
Healthier versions use baking instead of deep‑frying and whole‑grain breading.
Nuggets are a staple of many kids' menus, though they can contain additives and preservatives.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Chicken meat is rich in complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Nuggets provide niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: They contain iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood health and bones.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: With the right breading, nuggets can fit into low‑carbohydrate diets.

items.title: Satisfying crunch
items.content: The crispy coating and juicy interior help promote a feeling of fullness.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Deep‑fried nuggets can be calorie‑dense and contain saturated fats.

items.title: Additives and preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions often include flavor enhancers, artificial flavors and preservatives.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The breading is usually salted, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve nuggets hot, typically with a dipping sauce. They can be added to salads, wraps, or used as a protein boost in various dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen nuggets in an airtight bag in the freezer for up to 6 months. Cooked nuggets stored in the refrigerator should be consumed within 2 days.
